title: Tenant-slice temporal roles and breakglass admin model
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Design a role model that supports tenant-scoped role slices, temporal scopes (time-limited grants), delegated roles, and a controlled breakglass (emergency admin) pathway integrated with audit logging and SAML provisioning.

Context: Current RBAC in Redwood is flat and permission-centric; we need an RBAC v2 that maps to our multi-tenant resource hierarchy (Organization -> Project -> Model -> Deployment) and supports:
- role slices: the ability to attach a role to a subset of resources (label selectors + explicit resource lists)
- temporal scopes: short-lived grants (e.g., 4 hours) for on-call or contractor access
- delegation: principals can delegate a subset of their role to others with constraints
- breakglass: emergency elevation with strict approvals and automatic revoke + extended audit retention
- SAML/SCIM provisioning: map IdP groups to role templates with optional temporal overrides

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement the runtime enforcement hooks nor the console UI flows. Those will be separate tickets. This is the canonical model and migration plan for existing roles.

Design components:
1) Core primitives: RoleTemplate, RoleBinding, ScopeDescriptor, TemporalGrant, DelegationRecord, BreakglassRequest. Each primitive is a definition (schema) not an object graph. RoleTemplate is an ordered list of permission atoms (e.g., inference:invoke, admin:billing:view) and allowed resource masks. RoleBinding binds a RoleTemplate to a principal (user/service) and one or more ScopeDescriptors. ScopeDescriptor supports: explicit resource IDs, resource label selector, and pre-defined containers (e.g., entire Org or Project). TemporalGrant decorates RoleBinding with start/end timestamps and an issuing principal.

2) Inheritance and resolution rules:
- Most-specific scope wins when evaluating permission: explicit resource ID > label selector > container.
- Conflicts: DENY rules can be attached at the tenant-level. Any DENY with matching scope overrides allows. We will avoid complex policy language in v1, sticking to allow/deny + scope resolution by hierarchy.

3) Delegation model:
- Principals with delegatable flag on RoleTemplate can create bounded RoleBindings for others. Delegated bindings record origin binding id and maximum lifetime. Delegation chain length is limited to 2.

4) Breakglass controls:
- BreakglassRequest requires: requesting principal, justification, duration (max 12 hours), and approver (auto-approver allowed for SRE rotation with 2FA).
- On approval, a special short-lived binding is created with audit metadata and a high-fidelity log stream and retention (90 days by default). Post-expiration the binding is soft-deleted and an incident is created linking the breakglass event to the approvals.

5) Audit & observability:
- Every RoleBinding creation/update/expiry/actuation emits an AuditEvent with fields: actor, principal, binding_id, template_id, scope, temporal_window, reason, origin (UI/API/SAML). AuditEvents will include a pre/post ACL snapshot to aid investigations.
- Breakglass events produce an enriched AuditEvent with approver chain and signed nonce. We will add a dedicated dashboard and a PagerDuty alert for breakglass approvals in the first 30 days of rollout.

6) SAML/SCIM integration:
- SAML group->RoleTemplate mappings support optional TTL overrides (e.g., contractor groups become 24h). Mappings are stored as ProvisioningRules with priority. SCIM user provisioning will optionally create a RoleBinding with a TemporalGrant.

Migration plan:
- Phase 0 (read-only): export current RBAC to RoleTemplate candidates and detect ambiguous mappings.
- Phase 1 (dual-write): new RBAC store introduced; writes from console/API write both old and new representations and emit warnings.
- Phase 2 (read-migration): resolve conflicts and slowly flip read path for new APIs.
- Phase 3 (full-cutover): deprecate old model and remove legacy checks.

Rollout gating:
- Integration test coverage for permission resolution (100% for critical paths)
- Backend performance benchmark: permission evaluation must be < 3ms p95 for typical requests
- Security review and tabletop for breakglass flows

Trade-offs considered:
- We kept scope descriptors simple (no arbitrary boolean logic) to reduce evaluation complexity and caching explosion.
- Limiting delegation depth reduces correctness surface and simplifies revocation logic.
- DENY semantics at tenant-level chosen to support compliance use-cases but increases complexity for admins; we will monitor admin support metrics.

Open questions:
- Should temporal grants be renewable automatically with an approver? (needs PM sign-off)
- Retention window for breakglass audit data - compliance might request longer than 90 days.

Output artifacts: role-model ERD, permission atom catalog, JSON schema for each primitive, migration scripts, and example SAML mapping docs. See attachments for links.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical schema JSON definitions for RoleTemplate, RoleBinding, ScopeDescriptor, TemporalGrant, DelegationRecord, BreakglassRequest
Permission resolution algorithm documented (pseudocode) with complexity analysis
Migration plan with phased steps and rollback criteria
Audit event schema defined and example payloads for RoleBinding lifecycle and breakglass
SAML mapping examples and SCIM provisioning samples
Security review scheduled and checklist items enumerated
